# Manifest reference

livery reads one manifest, `livery.yaml`. It holds the config values and says which files to generate from them.

```yaml
version: 1

config:
  common:
    app_name: Demo
    api:
      url: https://api.example.com
  android:
    app_id: com.example.demo

outputs:
  android:
    merge: [common, android]
    files: [android/livery.properties]
```

Running `dart run livery` writes `android/livery.properties`:

```properties
# GENERATED BY livery. Do not edit by hand.
# Regenerate with `dart run livery`.

app_name=Demo
api_url=https://api.example.com
app_id=com.example.demo
```

Every mapping in the manifest accepts only the keys listed here. An unknown key, such as a misspelt `formt:`, fails generation and names the key and the keys accepted in its place. The keys inside `config` sections are your own data and are not checked.

All checks run before any file is written, so a failing run writes nothing.

## Finding the manifest

livery uses the file passed with `--config`, or else looks for `livery.yaml` in the working directory and then in each parent directory.

## Top level

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | int | `1` | Manifest format version. Only `1` is supported. |
| `root` | string | `.` | Directory that output paths resolve against, relative to the manifest. `--root` on the command line replaces it, resolved against the working directory. |
| `config` | mapping | empty | Config sections, see below. |
| `outputs` | mapping | required | The files to generate, see below. At least one output is required. |

### `root`

Use `root` when the manifest does not live at the top of the project:

```yaml
# tools/livery.yaml
root: ../app
```

## `config`

Each key of `config` is a **section**, a mapping of values that outputs merge. Section names are your own choice: `common`, `ios` and `android` are a convention, not a rule.

Values can be nested to any depth. A value is a string, a number, a boolean, `null` or a list.

## `outputs`

Each key of `outputs` names one output: the sections it merges, the format it is written in and the files it is written to.

```yaml
outputs:
  android:
    merge: [common, android]
    format: properties
    files:
      - android/livery.properties
      - android/app/livery.properties
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merge` | list of strings | the section named after the output | Sections merged left to right. Nested mappings merge key by key; any other value, lists included, is replaced by a later section. |
| `format` | string | `properties` | How the output is written. See [Formats](#formats). |
| `files` | string or list of strings | required | Destination paths, relative to `root`. Every file gets the same content. |

A format can accept further keys, listed with the format.

Rules for outputs:

- Every section in `merge` must exist in `config`.
- A path in `files` must be relative and must stay inside `root`, also after `..` segments are resolved.
- Two outputs, or two entries of one output, cannot write the same path.

A file whose content has not changed is not rewritten, so Xcode and Gradle do not rebuild for nothing.

## Formats

### `properties`

Java-style `key=value` lines, as Gradle's `Properties` reads them. The file starts with a "GENERATED BY livery" comment.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flatten` | bool | `true` | Join nested keys into one key. With `false`, every value must sit directly in a merged section. |
| `separator` | string | `_` | Joins the segments of a nested key: `api: {url: …}` becomes `api_url`. |

Values are written as text. `null` becomes an empty value and a list becomes its items joined by commas.

Keys and values are escaped so that `Properties.load` reads back exactly the configured text:

| In | Written as |
| --- | --- |
| `.` in a key | `__` |
| `\` | `\\` |
| line feed, carriage return, tab, form feed | `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\f` |
| space, `=`, `:` in a key | `\ `, `\=`, `\:` |
| space at the start of a value | `\ ` |
| `#` or `!` at the start of a key or value | `\#`, `\!` |

Two config keys that end up as the same key, such as `app: {name: …}` next to `app_name: …`, fail generation instead of one silently replacing the other.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | The manifest is invalid, or a file could not be read or written. |
| `64` | Bad command line usage. |
